clue.text: Having a different view of earth, for one?

definitions.note: a phrase describing the state; the answer is the noun for it

parts.note: surface reading: holding a new opinion about the planet
setter's reading: the word earth is what you get by rearranging the letters of the organ in the chest, so it is one example of that organ altered

explanation.surface: Someone who has come to see the planet differently, perhaps converted to green politics.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is CHANGE OF HEART: EARTH is an anagram of HEART, so earth is literally a changed heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A change of heart is an idiom for a reversal of opinion or feeling about something.

clue.text: Robust measure taken about blue movie with many cuts

indicators.note: taken about means wrapped around something, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: hale means healthy and strong
an en is a printer's unit of measure
feeling blue is feeling low

explanation.surface: A tough censor wields the scissors on a pornographic film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue movie' suggests pornography, but the movie is the horror film, and its cuts are slashes. The robust measure is split to let blue in.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloween is the 1978 slasher film, whose killer makes many knife cuts.

clue.text: Famous prize briefly in possession of one proud mum

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so one piece sits within the other
briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the Nobel Prize, the best-known award of all
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mother proudly shows off the famous prize her child has won.
explanation.walkthrough: NOBEL shortened to NOBE holds I after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Niobe boasted of her many children over Leto's and was punished by losing them all.

clue.text: Issuing magazine about Tirpitz — initially in German

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: Time, the American news magazine

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of the battleship's name
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A wartime magazine publishes a German-language article about the battleship Tirpitz.
explanation.definitionFit: Emitting means sending out or giving forth, the same as issuing.

clue.text: Was a servant at Eton whacked?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: at English public schools a junior boy served a senior as his fag
second meaning: British slang for exhausted

explanation.walkthrough: Eton is an elite English boarding school; 'whacked' reads as beaten with a cane, but it is slang for worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: To fag was to act as a younger pupil's servant to an older one; fagged also means tired out, just as whacked does.

clue.text: Giving knowledge training guidance and tuition primarily

indicators.note: training shapes something into a new form, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

indicators.note: primarily points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of tuition

explanation.surface: A description of teaching: training, guidance and above all tuition.
explanation.definitionFit: Educating is imparting learning to someone, which is a synonym for giving them knowledge.

clue.text: Going north and south girl breaks posh car's tracking device

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece enters the other
in a down entry, reading the same going up and going down means the word is identical both ways

parts.note: first half of RR, Rolls-Royce, the posh car
a girl's name
second half of RR

explanation.surface: A girl joyriding in a posh car breaks into its satnav.
explanation.walkthrough: RR (Rolls-Royce) is split by ADA, giving a word that reads the same up or down the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar locates and follows aircraft or ships by reflected radio waves, so it is a tracking system.

clue.text: Having this wisdom, sets out what crew should do

parts.note: to set out a case is to state it
a crew's job is to man the ship

explanation.surface: A wise captain explains to sailors what their duties are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sets out' looks like an anagram signal but means declares; 'what crew should do' is a phrase, MAN SHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Statesmanship is skill and sound judgment in managing public affairs, a kind of political wisdom.

clue.text: A jolly smooth hunk introduces start of this play

indicators.note: introducing something means bringing it in ahead of yourself, so that piece comes just before

parts.note: taken as written
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, RM
to sand wood is to smooth it

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of this
a he-man is a muscular hunk

explanation.surface: A cheerful, suave hunk opens the show in this play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' is a crossword favourite for a Royal Marine. The hunk puts the T in front of himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms and the Man is George Bernard Shaw's 1894 comedy, an example of a stage work.

clue.text: After end of Advent everyone's in debt and putting on fat

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of Advent
everyone is all
someone in debt is owing money

explanation.surface: After Christmas everybody is broke and has gained weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts T first in this charade.
explanation.definitionFit: To tallow is an old verb for growing fat, as livestock do; tallow is rendered animal fat.

clue.text: Neat place to get milk

parts.note: surface reading: a tidy little shop or dairy where you buy milk
setter's reading: neat is an old word for cattle, so this is the part of a cow that the milk comes from

explanation.walkthrough: Neat means cattle (as in neat's-foot oil), not tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: The udder is the bag-like mammary gland of a cow, where milk is drawn by milking.

clue.text: Tried really hard but not starting to get gold etc

indicators.note: not starting means the word goes without its opening letter

parts.note: strove is the past tense of strive

explanation.surface: Someone who made a huge effort but fell at the first hurdle in winning gold medals.
explanation.definitionFit: A trove is a store of treasure, such as gold, silver and jewels discovered together.

clue.text: Reference work including the end of many old beasts

parts.note: taken as written
the ending of many dinosaur names, like brontosaurus

explanation.surface: A reference book that covers the extinction of prehistoric animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The end of' looks like a last-letter signal, but here the end is the whole suffix shared by dinosaur names.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a book listing words grouped by meaning, a standard work you consult.

clue.text: Doing this, niggles England's tailender rudely

definitions.text: Doing this, niggles England's tailender rudely

indicators.note: rudely suggests roughly handled, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

indicators.note: the tail end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of England

explanation.surface: A fielder taunts England's last batsman with rude remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer. In cricket a tailender is a weak batsman low in the order, and sledging is verbally needling the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sledging is the cricket practice of insulting or taunting an opponent to break their concentration.

clue.text: For the pub trendy old man gets clothed in good material

indicators.note: being clothed in something means being wrapped by it, so these pieces go inside

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
something trendy is in
pa is a father
lace is a delicate fabric

explanation.surface: Dad dresses up in a smart outfit for a night at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The good material is split into its two parts, the abbreviation and the fabric, with the trendy old man between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin palace was a gaudily decorated Victorian pub selling gin, hence any showy bar.

clue.text: Note officer attached to poet

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant
one thing on another is attached to it

explanation.surface: A message from a military officer is pinned to a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: John Milton, author of Paradise Lost, is one of England's great poets.

clue.text: Come out, as printer arranged

indicators.note: arranged means put into a set order, so the letters are placed afresh

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material
taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: Pages emerge just as the printer has laid them out.
explanation.definitionFit: When a fact transpires it becomes known, emerging into the open.

clue.text: One might repair paintings on shop floor, finally

parts.note: re means on the subject of
a store is a shop

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: last letter of floor

explanation.surface: A conservator touches up pictures on the sales floor of a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A restorer is a conservator who cleans and repairs damaged artworks.

clue.text: Protection provided by pawn in gambit

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: In chess, a pawn sacrificed in an opening gambit shields the king.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canopy that gives shelter from sun or rain.

clue.text: Soldier, say, follows Russian NCO

indicators.note: follows means coming after, so the soldier's piece is placed behind the Russian's

parts.note: Serge, a Russian man's name, the form of Sergei
a soldier ant is one kind of ant

explanation.surface: A soldier follows a Russian sergeant's orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' looks like the definition beside NCO, but it is a kind of insect here.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a non-commissioned officer, the rank above corporal.

clue.text: Support the Queen's composer

parts.note: a bra is a support garment
HM, Her Majesty, plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: Backing the monarch's court musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms was a German Romantic composer of symphonies and the German Requiem.

clue.text: Out of sorts opera star gets the bird!

indicators.note: out of sorts means not in proper order, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material
taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: A diva off form is booed off the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets the bird' is a theatre idiom for being booed, but the bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea parrot is a popular name for the puffin, whose bright beak looks parrot-like.

clue.text: Steps left out for reptile

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter named just before is taken away

parts.note: a ladder is a set of steps
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone left the steps out and a snake got in.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is Britain's only venomous snake, a reptile also called the viper.

clue.text: Girl starts to slip under stool in eatery

indicators.note: starts means the opening letters of each of the following words

parts.note: the first letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: A young woman loses her footing beneath a bar stool in a café.
explanation.definitionFit: Susie is a girl's first name, a pet form of Susan.

clue.text: There's a lot of tape around old patient

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece goes inside the other
a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to tape something is to stick it
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A long-suffering hospital patient is wrapped in bandage tape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' is the adjective, not a person in hospital. STIC (from STICK) goes around O.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic person endures pain or hardship without complaint, so is patient in adversity.

clue.text: How Delia may describe the Spanish country?

parts.words: How Delia may describe the Spanish
parts.note: the name Delia is D and IA with EL, Spanish for the, sitting in between

explanation.surface: A cookery writer is asked how she would sum up Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer is the instruction that would build DELIA from EL. Delia Smith is a famous British TV cook.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a large nation of South Asia.

clue.text: Instrument hurt girl during broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means put out over the air, so the words are judged by their spoken sound

parts.note: harm is hurt and Monica is a girl's name; said together they run into one word

explanation.surface: A girl is injured in the middle of a live radio programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica is a mouth organ, a small wind instrument played by blowing and sucking.

clue.text: Very sad when one's late

parts.note: surface reading: unhappy because of arriving after time
setter's reading: late also means dead, so this is how one feels in mourning

explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' looks like tardy, but in 'the late Mr X' it means deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: Grief-stricken describes someone overwhelmed with sorrow, typically after a bereavement.
